'''Andrew Zbigniew Szydlo''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ʃ|ɪ|d|l|oʊ}} {{respell|SHID-low}}; born 1949) is a British [[chemist]] and [[chemistry teacher]] of Polish descent. Born in [[London]], he is best known for his talks and lectures on chemistry.

==Early life and education==
Szydlo was born in London, England to Polish parents, [[:pl:Kazimierz Szydło|Kazimierz]] and Daniela (née Suchecka). Daniela was one of many Polish children who were forcibly expatriated to [[Siberia]] by Soviet forces in 1942, and her experiences as an orphaned child in [[India]] have been described in an interview which she gave in 2011<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bkw_wyir_Ls |title=DANIELA SZYDLO z d. SUCHECKA. Polacy z Indii 1942-1948. |date=2025-10-03 |last=Polacy-z-Indii |access-date=2025-11-13 |via=YouTube}}</ref> and also in the book Poles in India.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Second World War Story - Poles in India 1942-1948 - Based on Archive Documents and Personal Reminiscences |publisher=[[Association of Poles in India 1942-1948]] |year=2015 |isbn=9780953892839 |edition=1st |location=London}}</ref> Szydlo attended Ellerslie Junior Mixed School in [[Shepherd's Bush]], followed by [[Latymer Upper School]], and then [[Imperial College London]] and [[University College London]]. 

He holds MSc, PhD, [[Diploma of Imperial College|DIC]], [[ACGI]], and is a [[Royal Society of Chemistry|Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]].

An expert on the history of [[alchemy]], Szydlo is the author of the standard work on the Polish alchemist, [[Michael Sendivogius]]. The thesis of his book ''"Water that does not wet hands": The Alchemy of Michael Sendivogius'',<ref>Published by the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] in 1994.</ref> which argues that Sendivogius' role in the discovery of [[oxygen]] has not received proper attention, has won widespread acceptance within the academic community.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} He advanced this argument in a leading article for ''[[History Today]]'', co-authored with [[Richard Brzezinski]], entitled "A New Light on Alchemy".<ref>Vol. 47, issue 1: http://www.historytoday.com/MainArticle.aspx?m=13491&amid=13491</ref> His work on seventeenth-century science is an ongoing project to which he hopes to devote further attention.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}}

== Teaching career ==
He has taught [[chemistry]] at [[Highgate School]], an independent school in North London, since January 1975.<ref>https://uk.linkedin.com/pub/andrew-szydlo/86/1b9/526 LinkedIn Entry. Retrieved 15 June 2015. –  September 1972 – December 1974: Chemistry, ''Science'', DT, Mathematics at Cardinal Manning School, Highgate School;  Jan 1975 – today: Chemistry at Highgate School</ref> He currently teaches children as part of the school's community engagement programme.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Partnerships |url=https://www.highgateschool.org.uk/our-community/partnerships/ |access-date=2025-11-13 |website=Highgate School |language=en-GB}}</ref> In 2020, Szydlo was awarded a Pearson National Teaching award for Lifetime Achievement.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.teachingawards.com/award-winner/dr-andrew-szydlo/|title = Dr Andrew Szydlo}}</ref>

In 2015 he published ''Schoolmaster's Diary'', a photo diary celebrating four decades of school life seen through his chemistry teacher's lens.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://metro.co.uk/2015/11/26/chemistry-teachers-photo-diary-celebrates-four-decades-of-school-life-and-epic-haircuts-5527687/|title=Chemistry teacher's epic photo diary celebrates four decades in the classroom|date=26 November 2015}}</ref>

== Public engagement ==
He frequently gives public lectures in the United Kingdom on topics including the [[History of Chemistry]]. Select notable performances include those at [[Cambridge University]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://talks.cam.ac.uk/talk/index/12836.htm|title=talks.cam : Fireworks and Waterworks! Lecture & demonstration.|publisher=University of Cambridge}}</ref> [[Durham University]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/events/|title=Conferences and events|website=rsc.org}}</ref> [[University College London]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.chem.ucl.ac.uk/schools/events.html |title=UCL Chemistry – Contact Pages |access-date=11 April 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060925144615/http://www.chem.ucl.ac.uk/schools/events.html |archive-date=25 September 2006 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the [[Royal Institution]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.rigb.org/contentControl?action=displayEvent&id=837 |title=The Royal Institution of Great Britain &#124; Schools event: As if by magic |access-date=10 April 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110612053325/http://www.rigb.org/contentControl?action=displayEvent&id=837 |archive-date=12 June 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Cheltenham Science Festival]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cheltenhamfestivals.com/news/2013/12/science-and-maths-festive-extravaganzas-bring-the-fun-of-the-science-festival-to-pupils-across-the-country/|title=Science and maths festive extravaganzas|website=Cheltenham Festivals}}</ref> and [[Hampton Court]].<ref name="science1">{{cite web|url=http://guerillascience.org/|title=Home|first=Guerilla|last=Science|website=Guerilla Science}}</ref> These have received much acclaim: writing in the journal ''[[Chemistry & Industry]]'' on Szydlo's performance at Cambridge, John Wilkins remarked that "Dr Szydlo exceeded all expectations; he raced through vast tracts of practical chemistry, history, alchemy, the discovery of oxygen, the [[internal combustion engine]], and on occasion, introduced music too. His lecture was interspersed with flashes, bangs, colour changes, detonations and eruptions, keeping the 350-strong crowd on the edge of their seats throughout." This lively, multi-media approach characterises Szydlo's performances, which include experiments drawn from a wide repertory, ranging from the chemistry of colour to pyrotechnics and high explosives. He has also appeared at several festivals as part of the Guerilla Science team.<ref name="science1"/> He also lectures regularly at schools throughout the United Kingdom, and has remarked that he often finds the audiences he addresses at under-privileged schools the most inspiring.<ref>Personal communication with the author.</ref> These lectures are sometimes featured in the local press.<ref>e.g. 'Smoke and steam fire up and enthusiasm for science', Ham & High, 12 March 2009.</ref> Szydlo also regularly gives talks for the wider community, including such institutions as the [[Stuart Low Trust]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slt.org.uk/?s=szydlo|title=Search Results for "szydlo" – The Stuart Low Trust}}</ref> [[Haringey Council]] Cared for Children, and the [[Polish Scouting and Guiding Association]]. His recent{{When|date=May 2026}} webinars for students in [[Turkey]] and [[Tunisia]] have been very well received.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=khFBDxe33f4 | title="Mystery of Chemistry" Webinar by Dr. Andrew Szydlo &#124; ChemTalk' #2 | website=[[YouTube]] | date=3 May 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.linkedin.com/posts/aymenlabidy_its-with-great-honor-and-privilege-for-me-activity-6950725424423301120-XJxl | title=It's with great honor and privilege for me to be the coordinator and – Aymen Labidi on LinkedIn }}</ref> He has also been invited to give numerous lectures and demonstrations abroad, including Poland, [[Mauritius]]<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hM2slt7I_Bc |title=Dr. Andrew Szydlo - The Magic behind my Chemistry Talks |date=2019-02-26 |last=Café Scientifique Maurice |access-date=2025-11-13 |via=YouTube}}</ref> and [[Namibia]].

He has collaborated with [[Andrea Sella]] of University College London and the author [[Hugh Aldersey-Williams]] in ''Elements'', an exhibition at the [[Wellcome Collection]],<ref>{{cite web |date=14 March 2011 |title=Kill or cure? It's elementary at Wellcome Collection's late event – Wellcome |url=https://wellcome.ac.uk/press-release/kill-or-cure-its-elementary-wellcome-collections-late-event |website=wellcome.ac.uk}}</ref> where he spoke about the Dutch alchemist [[Cornelis Drebbel]], situating Drebbel in a broader scientific and historical context and illustrating the talk with lively experiments.<ref>{{cite news |date=12 April 2011 |title=Elements explode at new science exhibition |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/elements-explode-at-new-science-exhibition-2266647.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220507/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/elements-explode-at-new-science-exhibition-2266647.html |archive-date=7 May 2022 |website=The Independent}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Aldersey-Williams has worked with Szydlo before, both as a pupil at [[Highgate School]], where he recalls Szydlo as 'a man of many talents ... always liable to whip out his gipsy violin mid-lesson',<ref>Hugh Aldersey-Williams, ''Periodic Tales: the curious lives of the elements'', Viking (2011), pp. 120–123</ref> and in writing his book ''Periodic Tales'', when he recruited Szydlo's expertise in an attempt to recreate the experiment that discovered [[phosphorus]].

[[File:Andrew Szydlo experiment for LIYSF.jpg|right|thumb|Szydlo performing an experiment with gases in 2021]]
He has appeared in six television serials: as a chemistry teacher in ''That'll Teach 'em'' ([[Channel 4]], 2006)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0813905/|title=That'll Test 'Em|publisher=IMDb}}</ref> and ''Sorcerer's Apprentice'' ([[CBBC]], 2007);<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b007t0wc/episodes/guide|title=Sorcerer's Apprentice – Next on – BBC – CBBC|publisher=BBC}}</ref> as a science historian in ''Absolute Zero'' (BBC4, 2007);<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/bbcfour/documentaries/features/absolute-zero.shtml |title=BBC – BBC Four Documentaries – Absolute Zero |access-date=25 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111114222034/http://www.bbc.co.uk/bbcfour/documentaries/features/absolute-zero.shtml |archive-date=14 November 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> as a chemist in ''Generals at War'' (National Geographic, 2009);<ref>{{cite web|url=http://natgeotv.com.au/tv/generals-at-war/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110409005123/http://natgeotv.com.au/tv/generals-at-war/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=9 April 2011 |title=Generals at War – National Geographic |publisher=Natgeotv.com.au |access-date=26 May 2019}}</ref> in ''Big, Bigger, Biggest'' ([[Channel 5 (British TV channel)|Channel 5]], 2009);<ref>{{cite web |url=https://channel.nationalgeographic.com/ |title=Channel Homepage |website=National Geographic Channel |access-date=26 May 2019 |archive-date=2 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702115933/http://channel.nationalgeographic.com/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> and as "The Doc" in ''Secrets of Everything'' ([[BBC3]], 2012).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b012zyk7|title=BBC Three – The Secrets of Everything|publisher=BBC}}</ref>

== Wider specialities ==
Andrew Szydlo is an accomplished player of instruments including the violin, piano, bugle and accordion.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} The string quartet ''[[Alchymic Quartet]]'' by [[Graham Waterhouse]], whom he taught at Highgate School and has maintained a friendship with since, was inspired by his chemical experiments,<ref name="GW60">{{cite web
| url = https://www.arbc.de/Waterhouse/pdf/2022-11-05%20GW60.pdf
| title = GW60 – Festkonzert
| website = Graham Waterhouse
| date = 2022
| language = de
| pages = 4, 11
| access-date = 8 December 2022
}}</ref> which he performed them for the premiere of the quartet in November 2022.<ref name="Gilching">{{cite web
| url = https://www.gilching-news.de/landpartie-mit-neuer-musik/
| title = Landpartie mit "neuer" Musik
| website = [[Gilching]]
| date = 26 October 2022
| language = de
| access-date = 28 December 2022
}}</ref> Szydlo also has considerable expertise in photography.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} He has exhibited his own photographs, and recently contributed a preface to a book of photographs published by the artist [[Stephane Graff]].<ref>Stephane Graff, ''Professore'', Istanbul (2010)</ref> His other interests include Polish dancing, [[Automotive engineering|automobile engineering]], [[meteorology]], [[beekeeping]], and [[mycology]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} Amongst his pupils, he is renowned for lessons which incorporate unusual and spectacular experiments, and for bursts of theatricality such as blowing fire and cooling hot drinks with [[liquid nitrogen]] before tasting them. His lecture and television performances reflect his broad cultural interests and distinctive character.

Szydlo has the highest rank ([[Harcmistrz]]) in the [[Polish Scouting Association]], and has regularly participated in its activities since 1965. Szydlo's account of one of his cub scout meetings from 1971 has recently{{When|date=May 2026}} been made into a documentary film by John Chrzanowski.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chrzanowski |first=John |title= |url=https://www.facebook.com/reel/1133260629006145 |access-date=13 November 2025 |website=[[Facebook]]}}</ref>

At Highgate School, he runs an automotive engineering society where he teaches students using old [[Triumph Herald]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-02 |title=Five minutes with: Dr Andrew Szydlo {{!}} Highgate Voices |url=https://www.highgateschool.org.uk/news/highgate-voices/five-minutes-with-dr-andrew-szydlo/ |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=Highgate School |language=en-GB}}</ref> He has published award-winning articles reflecting on his adventures.
